newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul shrs plunge by close on interest concerns.
newsitem.headline: Seoul shrs plunge by close on interest concerns.

text.p: Worries about rising market interest rates took their toll on Seoul stocks, pushing the index to a sharply lower close, brokers said on Friday.
The composite stock index plummeted 24.41 points or 3.43 percent to 686.72. Losers led gainers by 724 to 110.
"Many investors are worried about gradually rising interest rates and they believe there will be further rises," said Hwang Chang-joong of LG Securities.
The concerns stemmed from news that the Korea Securities Deales Association received a record 3.91 trillion won worth of new corporate bond issue applications for next month.
Yields on three-year corporate bonds climbed near 12.50 percent level from Thursday's close of 12.32 percent.

Brokers said blue chips spearheaded the index fall as those firms were anticipated to come up with much worse-than-expected corporate results for calendar 1996. Many South Korean companies planned to hold shareholders meeting next week, when profit and loss statement would be revealed.
Korea Mobile Telecom went limit down, losing 43,000 won to 495,000. "Some institutions began selling Korea Mobile and this sparked across the board sales," said Woo Sang-chul of Tongyang Securities.
DACOM shed 8,000 won to 104,000 and Samsung Electronics lost 3,600 won to 53,000.
Brokers said slipping customers' deposit at brokerage houses also pressured investor sentiment.
Sewon went limit up in early trading as Miwon began buying Sewon shares to merge the two companies. But it hit lower limit of 72,300, down 6,200 at the close.
Brokers forecast the market would consolidate next week. "I expect no big rally until mid-March," Woo said.
